subject: Science
title: Year 9 Science Exam 6
topic: Inheritance · Chemical reactions · Investigative skills · AQA Higher
intro: You may use a calculator. For longer answers write in full sentences and use key words. Describe = say what happens; Explain = say what happens and why (use because and so); Compare = similarities and differences (use whereas); Evaluate = points for and against, then a justified conclusion. 6-mark questions are marked on how well your ideas link together: plan for a minute, then write about 6 linked points. Show your working for calculations. Relative atomic masses (Aᵣ): H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23, Mg = 24, S = 32, Cl = 35.5, Ca = 40, Fe = 56.

questions.q: Where are genes found?
questions.ms: B1: on chromosomes in the nucleus. A gene is a short section of DNA on a chromosome.

questions.q: What is a mutation?
questions.ms: B1: a change in the DNA. Mutations make new alleles, which cause variation.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of continuous variation?
options: Whether you can roll your tongue
questions.ms: B1: arm length. It can be any value in a range; the others fall into separate groups.

questions.q: What is the ratio of hydrogen : sulfur : oxygen atoms in sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄?
Which of these is an abiotic factor?
questions.ms: B1: soil pH. Abiotic factors are non-living; the others are living (biotic).

questions.q:
Cystic fibrosis is an inherited disorder caused by a recessive allele (f). The dominant allele (F) does not cause the disorder.
Two parents are both carriers (Ff). Use a Punnett square for this cross. Type the gametes of each parent and the genotypes of the four offspring.
questions.ms: B1: gametes F and f from each parent. B1: offspring FF, Ff, Ff, ff.

questions.q: What is the percentage chance that their child will have cystic fibrosis? (%)
questions.ms: Answer: 25%. B1 (1 out of 4 offspring is ff).

questions.q: What is the expected ratio of children without cystic fibrosis to children with cystic fibrosis?
questions.ms: B1: 3 : 1 (FF, Ff, Ff do not have it; ff has it).

questions.q: Explain why the parents do not have cystic fibrosis, even though they each carry the allele for it.
questions.ms: B1: the allele for cystic fibrosis is recessive. B1: they also have one dominant allele (F), which is enough to stop the disorder showing; a person needs two copies of f (ff) to have it.

questions.q:
MRSA is a type of bacteria that is resistant to many antibiotics.
Explain how a population of antibiotic-resistant bacteria develops, and why doctors ask patients to finish their course of antibiotics.
questions.ms: 6 marks, level-marked. Level 3 (5-6 marks): a detailed, logically linked answer covering most points. Level 2 (3-4 marks): several relevant points, some linked. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple, separate statements. Indicative content: a random mutation in the DNA of a bacterium makes it resistant to the antibiotic; there is variation in the population; when the antibiotic is used, the bacteria without the mutation are killed; the resistant bacteria survive; they reproduce (very quickly, by splitting) and pass on the resistance allele/gene; the population of resistant bacteria grows; this is natural selection; the antibiotic no longer works against them; finishing the course kills all the bacteria, so none survive to mutate or become resistant; not over-prescribing (e.g. not for viral infections) also reduces resistance.

questions.q: Some plant species are at risk of extinction. Describe how a seed bank (a type of gene bank) can help to stop a plant species becoming extinct.
questions.ms: B1: seeds of the species are collected and stored (cold and dry, so they stay alive for a long time). B1: if the plants die out in the wild, the seeds can be grown and replanted. B1: it keeps the genetic variation / different alleles of the species, e.g. alleles for disease resistance, for the future.

questions.q:
Biodiversity is the variety of all the different species in an area. The UAE has protected areas such as the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary.
Describe and explain two ways that people can help to maintain biodiversity.
questions.ms: For each of two ways: B1 the method and B1 the explanation. E.g. protecting habitats / nature reserves, so species have food and shelter and are not disturbed; breeding programmes for endangered species, so their numbers increase; replanting hedgerows / mangroves / forests, so more species have places to live; reducing pollution or deforestation, so fewer habitats are destroyed; recycling, so less land is used for landfill.

questions.ms: Answer: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. B1.

questions.ms: Answer: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. B2. B1 for 2Fe₂O₃ with Fe balanced but O₂ wrong.

questions.q:
Magnesium burns in oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
Calculate the maximum mass of magnesium oxide that can be made from 6 g of magnesium. (g)
questions.ms: Answer: 10 g. M1 for Mᵣ of MgO = 40. M1 for 48 g of Mg makes 80 g of MgO (or 6 ÷ 24 = 0.25). A1 for 80 × 6 ÷ 48 = 10 g.

questions.q: A student burns 6 g of magnesium and collects 8.5 g of magnesium oxide. Calculate the percentage yield. (%)
questions.ms: Answer: 85%. M1 for 8.5 ÷ 10 × 100. A1 for 85. (Follow through from their answer to 12(a).)

questions.q: Give two reasons why the percentage yield is less than 100%.
questions.ms: B1 each for any two: some magnesium oxide escaped as white smoke when the lid was lifted; not all of the magnesium reacted (not heated for long enough); some product was left behind or spilled when it was moved or weighed; the magnesium was not pure / had an oxide coating already.

questions.q:
A student measures the hand span of 30 students in her year group. Her results are in the table.
Hand span (cm)16 to 1717 to 1818 to 1919 to 2020 to 21
Number of students371163

What type of variation is hand span?
questions.ms: B1: continuous. Hand span can be any value in a range.

questions.q: Which type of graph should she draw to show these results?
options: Bar chart with gaps between the bars
questions.ms: B1: histogram, because hand span is continuous data in groups, so the bars touch.

questions.q: Which group is the modal class (the most common)?
questions.ms: B1: 18 to 19 cm (11 students).

questions.q: Explain whether hand span is caused by inherited variation, environmental variation, or both.
questions.ms: B1: both. B1: genes inherited from parents control how large the hand can grow, and the environment (e.g. diet / nutrition, injury, sport) also affects it.

questions.q: Give one strength and one weakness of her investigation.
questions.ms: B1 strength, e.g. 30 students is a reasonable sample / all measured with the same ruler and method / results grouped clearly. B1 weakness, e.g. only one year group (all the same age) / sample too small to be sure about the whole school / measured to the nearest cm, so not very precise / different people stretch their hands differently.

questions.q:
Compare sexual and asexual reproduction.
In your answer, give advantages and disadvantages of each.
questions.ms: 6 marks, level-marked. A Level 3 answer gives similarities and differences, with advantages and disadvantages of both. Level 3 (5-6 marks): a detailed, logically linked answer covering most points. Level 2 (3-4 marks): several relevant points, some linked. Level 1 (1-2 marks): simple, separate statements. Indicative content: sexual reproduction needs two parents, whereas asexual needs only one; sexual involves gametes (sperm and egg) fusing in fertilisation, whereas asexual has no gametes; sexual produces offspring with variation (mix of genes from both parents), whereas asexual produces clones (genetically identical); ADVANTAGES of sexual: variation means some may survive a disease or change in the environment, which helps natural selection; DISADVANTAGES of sexual: needs to find a mate, takes more time and energy, fewer offspring; ADVANTAGES of asexual: fast, only one parent needed, many offspring, good characteristics copied exactly; DISADVANTAGES of asexual: no variation, so a disease or change in conditions could wipe out the whole population. Similarity: both produce new offspring / pass on DNA to the next generation.

questions.q:
Coral reefs in the Arabian Gulf are home to many species of fish.
Explain how one abiotic factor and one biotic factor could reduce the number of fish on a reef.
questions.ms: B1 abiotic factor, e.g. rising sea temperature / pollution / lower oxygen in the water / change in salt or pH. B1 explanation, e.g. hotter water kills the coral (coral bleaching), so fish lose food and shelter. B1 biotic factor, e.g. a new predator / a new disease / more competition for food / less food (fewer prey). B1 explanation, e.g. a new predator eats the fish, so fewer survive to reproduce.
